_readme: Resume state for the newsletter harvest (tools/upkeep-routine.md step 2).
Read this BEFORE a harvest pass; update `last_processed`/`count`/`updated` and COMMIT it after.
This file lives in the repo (not session memory) precisely so a CLOUD agent can clone, resume, and open a PR.
`react-brain lint` cross-checks each `count` against encyclopedia.yaml sources_digested — they must match.
Narrative harvest history (what each pass changed, process learnings) lives in tools/harvest-log/LEDGER.md — in-repo since 2026-08-07.

this-week-in-react.name: This Week in React
this-week-in-react.notes: issue pages fetch directly at /newsletter/{n} — BUT A 200 IS NOT PROOF OF PUBLICATION: cross-check the ARCHIVE listing at /newsletter or reject titles ending in ': ...' before treating an issue as live. That rule EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN on 2026-09-21: /newsletter/298 returned 200 while the archive listing ended at #297, and both its og:title and <h1> read literally '#298: ...' — a stub, exactly the 2026-08-18 #294 precedent. #297 (processed 2026-09-21) was the densest issue in months: 74 links, headlined by Shopify leaving React Native and Expo SDK 58 beta. #298 expected to go live within days

react-status.name: React Status
react-status.notes: corroboration-heavy; headliners usually already held. Probed FIRST per the standing note: #490 AND #491 were both live on 2026-09-21 and both processed. #490 originated the Tailwind-Labs-joins-Shopify keep; #491 originated the VITE DEV-SERVER CVE keep (CVE-2026-39364) — which sat FAR DOWN its link list and was only caught because the coverage gate demands a row per link. Lesson recorded: this source buries real finds below the headline items, so never triage it from the headlines alone. Next: probe #492 (publishes Thursdays)

react-digest.name: React Digest
react-digest.notes: issues slug-titled by featured article; article/depth-driven. Archive: /newsletters or /newsletters.rss (newest-first, resolves the slug) — /digests 404s. Slug numbers are NOT sequential (2344 → 2350 → 2355 → 2360 → 2365). #2365 ('The browser's main thread is expensive', processed 2026-09-21) yielded ZERO keeps — 12 links, half of them sibling-newsletter cross-promotion, and its React items (React 19.3, the Rust compiler post, a React-internals tutorial) were all already held. That is TWO consecutive zero-yield issues (#2360, #2365); if #2370 also yields zero, measure its origination rate the way React Weekly's was measured before deciding whether it earns its slot

react-native-rewind.name: React Native Rewind
react-native-rewind.notes: slug-titled; each issue page carries an authoritative 'Issue #NN' label near the title — use THAT, not sequential guesswork, to resume (verified again 2026-09-21: the two newest slugs labelled themselves #57 and #56). RSS at /newsletter-rss.xml (newest-first) 307-redirects — curl -L; canonical host is www.thereactnativerewind.com. #57 ('React Native is DEAD, Expo Modules 2.0, and a $49 Flutter knockoff') was almost entirely commentary on the Shopify announcement plus Expo Modules 2.0 — both kept from PRIMARY sources, so it originated nothing; its remaining links are background references (UIView, Yoga, Fabric, Impeller)

native-weekly.name: Native Weekly
native-weekly.notes: nativeweekly.com is a shell — use the beehiiv archive (slugs like /p/sep-11-2026-issue-20). NOTE THE SLUG TYPO TRAP: #21's slug reads 'sep-18-2025-issue-21' (2025, not 2026) — trust the issue number, not the date in the slug. Author also authors rnsec (watch self-promotion). Cadence has tightened to roughly fortnightly: #19 2026-08-28 → #20 2026-09-11 → #21 2026-09-18. Two issues processed 2026-09-21. The standing read holds: its release-roundup rows duplicate the firsthand watch almost entirely (#21 was ~20 npm/GitHub rows, all corroboration) and the ARTICLES are where its keeps are — #20 originated the Margelo-joins-Callstack keep, which no other source this pass carried

react-weekly.name: React Weekly
react-weekly.notes: RETIRED 2026-09-21 — do not process further issues; kept in this file so the ×30 count keeps matching encyclopedia sources_digested and the decision stays visible. The 2026-09-10 criterion was pre-committed precisely so this would not be re-argued from one quiet issue: 'if #37 also originates zero keeps, that is four consecutive and the structural argument is proven: drop it then.' Measured on 2026-09-21: #37 originated ZERO (all six links already-held or corroboration — jotai v3, RN 0.88-rc.0, the Rust-compiler post, Expo Modules 2.0, React 19.3, Expo Go login) and #38 originated ZERO (Shopify back-to-native, the KMP study, Discord New-Arch, SDK 58 — every one of them carried by TWiR #297 or already held). That is issues 34-38, FIVE consecutive with no origination, against a lifetime rate of 9 keeps / 65 rows (14%) across 29-36. The structural reason, now proven rather than suspected: its editorial is a subset of TWiR + the firsthand watch, and the overlap grew as firsthand coverage grew. IRREVERSIBILITY WARNING kept on the record: its RSS window is the latest 20 issues only, so this backlog becomes permanently unreachable (issues 1-7 already are). To resurrect it, re-measure origination over three fresh issues before trusting it again
